title: Mirage (মরীচিকা)
description: A mirage (pages 251–252, topic 9.2.2, চিত্র ৯.১০). A strip of desert sand with a few pebbles floats in a calm deep-blue setting; a coconut palm stands on the right and a textbook eye on a thin stand looks at it from the left (no face). Five steps, one tap each, slow: (1) the eye sees the tree directly along a straight amber ray; (2) the sun heats the sand and the book's three layers of air appear as faint tinted slabs with light boundary lines, labelled উপরের স্তর · n বেশি, মাঝের স্তর, নিচের স্তর · n কম (the book's simplification); (3) a second ray leaves the tree's top downward, the camera flies in, and at the first boundary the normal (অভিলম্ব) and the angles i and r show the angle of refraction growing, while at the second boundary the angle of incidence passes the critical angle (ক্রান্তি কোণ) and the ray is totally reflected (পূর্ণ অভ্যন্তরীণ প্রতিফলন); (4) it climbs to the eye, the eye's line is carried on dashed below the ground and an upside-down see-through palm appears there, labelled প্রতিবিম্ব (অবাস্তব), over a pale patch that looks like water; (5) the eye walks up to the tree: the ray has to come down steeply, its angle of incidence falls below the critical angle, it ends in the sand and the image and the 'water' vanish (মরীচিকাকে দূর থেকে দেখা যায়, কাছে এলে দেখা যায় না). Then the student drags the eye near and far and watches the mirage come and go, with the angle of incidence against the critical angle in the panel. Rays traced exactly with Snell's law per boundary; the index differences and the layers are exaggerated and say so. Calm intro card, one lead-in line, result and rule per step, the kit's how-to row, a five-question test. Phone-first, Bangla and English.
